physics_detail: Sr-90 → Y-90 + β⁻ + ν̄ₑ; E_max = 546 keV; Q-value = 546 keV; average beta energy ≈ 195 keV (~1/3 of E_max for allowed transitions); spectrum is CONTINUOUS from 0 to 546 keV (Fermi energy distribution); pure beta emitter = no gamma
chernobyl_relevance: Sr-90 emits only beta radiation → undetectable by standard gamma-sensitive Geiger-Müller counters and NaI detectors; this is why Sr-90 can be present in water/soil at hazardous levels with no gamma signal; requires Cherenkov counting or beta spectrometry for detection
source: NNDC NuDat 3; Fermi 1934 Z Physik; radioactive_decay_chains_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Y-90 → Zr-90 (stable) + β⁻ + ν̄ₑ; E_max = 2.279 MeV; average beta energy ≈ 933 keV; t1/2(Y-90)=64.1 hr; secular equilibrium with Sr-90 in environment; in equilibrium: Sr-90 and Y-90 activities equal
chernobyl_relevance: Y-90's 2.28 MeV beta produces Cherenkov radiation in water (visible blue light; threshold ~0.26 MeV for water); used for Cherenkov counting of Y-90 / Sr-90 in water samples; maximum range in tissue = 11 mm; can penetrate skin (dead layer ~70 µm); eye lens dose from Y-90 in contaminated water possible at high concentrations

physics_detail: Sr-90 beta max range in tissue (Csda range): ~1.8 mm at E_max=546 keV; Y-90 beta max range ~11 mm; both ranges much shorter than typical organ dimensions; dose deposited locally within ~1-2 cm of source
chernobyl_relevance: For Sr-90 in bone: beta irradiates immediately adjacent bone marrow; dose highly concentrated in trabecular bone surface cells and adjacent marrow cells; this is why Sr-90 bone dose coefficient is very high (Sr-90 is a bone-seeker replacing Ca)
source: NIST ESTAR electron stopping power; ICRP 67; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Cs-137 → Ba-137m (93.5%) + β⁻ + ν̄ₑ with E_max=514 keV; also Cs-137 → Ba-137 ground state (6.5%) with E_max=1174 keV; Ba-137m then emits 662 keV gamma (85.1%); average beta energy ≈ 188 keV for dominant branch
chernobyl_relevance: Cs-137 beta deposits dose locally (max range ~4 mm in tissue) while 662 keV gamma penetrates body; external Cs-137 exposure: skin beta dose is surface dose; whole-body dose from penetrating gamma; internally: Cs-137 uniformly distributed in soft tissue → whole-body irradiation from both beta and gamma

physics_detail: I-131 → Xe-131 + β⁻ + ν̄ₑ (dominant branch E_max=606 keV, 89.4%); followed by gamma 364.5 keV (81.5%); t1/2=8.02 days; average beta energy ~192 keV; range in thyroid tissue ~5 mm
chernobyl_relevance: I-131 beta deposits virtually all energy within thyroid gland (thyroid ~20g adult; ~4g infant); localized dose = HIGH dose per unit activity ingested; I-131 thyroid dose coefficient adult 4.3E-07 Sv/Bq; infant 2.4E-06 Sv/Bq; see dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Pu-239 → U-235 + α; E_alpha = 5.150 MeV (monoenergetic; discrete energy lines); t1/2=24110 yr; specific activity = 2.31 GBq/g; alpha particles are helium nuclei (2 protons + 2 neutrons); monoenergetic unlike continuous beta spectrum
chernobyl_relevance: Pu-239 alpha = LET ~80-100 keV/µm in tissue; range = 37 µm in tissue (< one cell diameter); completely stopped by dead layer of skin (70 µm); ONLY hazardous if inhaled or ingested (internal dose); RBE=20 for cancer induction; hot particles of Pu-239 create very concentrated local dose

physics_detail: Am-241 → Np-237 + α; dominant E_alpha = 5.486 MeV (85.2%) and 5.443 MeV (12.8%); t1/2=432.2 yr; specific activity = 127 GBq/g; also emits 59.54 keV gamma (35.9%) = detectable by gamma spectrometry; growing in Chernobyl environment from Pu-241 decay
chernobyl_relevance: Am-241 growing in CEZ soils (Bateman equations; peaks 2059); alpha from hot particles = internal hazard if inhaled; 59.54 keV gamma allows detection at surface but attenuated by >1 cm soil; alpha spectrometry (silicon surface barrier detector) detects alpha at 5.486 MeV; see am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Alpha particle range in tissue: 37 µm for 5.15 MeV Pu-239 alpha; 37 µm ≈ 2-3 cell diameters; dead skin layer (~70 µm) completely stops alpha from external contamination; this is why alpha emitters are ONLY dangerous internally (inhalation/ingestion)
chernobyl_relevance: For hot particle inhalation: Pu-239 alpha from hot particle deposits ALL energy within 37 µm radius; creates highly localized dose (hot spots) that are much more biologically effective than distributed dose of equal energy; single hot particle in lung can deliver Gy-level dose to adjacent cells; see fuel_particle_contamination_REAL.csv
source: NIST ASTAR; IAEA 1988 hot particles report; Casarett 1968; radiation_biology_mechanisms_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Cherenkov radiation: charged particle moving faster than light in medium (v > c/n where n=refractive index); threshold kinetic energy for electrons in water: E_k > 261 keV (n_water=1.34); visible blue glow; used for detection of Y-90 beta (E_max=2279 keV >> threshold)
chernobyl_relevance: Y-90 (E_max=2.28 MeV) easily exceeds Cherenkov threshold → allows sensitive counting of Sr-90/Y-90 in water without chemical separation; Cherenkov imaging used for spent fuel monitoring; Chernobyl cooling pond: irradiated fuel assemblies visible by Cherenkov glow
source: Frank IM Tamm IG 1937 Dokl Akad Nauk SSSR; Knoll 2010; rbmk_fuel_specifications_REAL.csv

physics_detail: Ba-137m can de-excite by: (1) gamma emission (662 keV; 85.1%); or (2) internal conversion (IC) where 662 keV energy transferred to K- or L-shell electron ejected with E = 662 - E_binding; K-shell IC electron: ~624 keV; L-shell IC: ~655 keV; IC coefficient ~0.11
chernobyl_relevance: Internal conversion electrons from Ba-137m contribute to skin dose from surface Cs-137 contamination; IC electrons range ~2 mm in tissue; along with Cs-137 beta these contribute to beta skin dose; important for skin contamination dosimetry
source: NNDC IC coefficient data; Attix 1986; dosimetry of external beta contamination

physics_detail: Standard Geiger-Müller tube: detects charged particles (electrons from beta decay or Compton electrons from gamma); THIN-WINDOW GM tube detects beta radiation; SHIELDED GM tube with gamma background counts = beta-gamma discrimination; Sr-90 pure beta = needs END-WINDOW or thin-window GM tube placed close to source
chernobyl_relevance: Soviet field monitoring 1986: used DP-5 and DP-100 instruments sensitive primarily to gamma; Sr-90 was INVISIBLE to these instruments; explains why Sr-90 contamination was systematically underestimated in 1986 monitoring; required separate beta-specific measurements

physics_detail: Bremsstrahlung (braking radiation): beta particles decelerate in Coulomb field of nuclei → emit continuous X-ray spectrum; intensity ∝ Z² × E_beta; significant for high-energy beta in high-Z materials; for Sr-90/Y-90 (E_max=2.28 MeV) in concrete/lead: bremsstrahlung can penetrate shielding
chernobyl_relevance: Practical consequence: shielding of pure beta emitters (Sr-90, Y-90) with high-Z material (lead) is counterproductive → use LOW-Z shielding (plastic, water, aluminum) first to absorb beta, then gamma shield for bremsstrahlung; relevant for CEZ waste container design
source: Attix 1986; NCRP Report 116; IAEA waste management guidance

physics_detail: Fermi coupling constant G_F/(ℏc)³ = 1.166×10⁻⁵ GeV⁻²; governs weak force interaction rate; determines beta decay half-lives; directly relates to why some isotopes (I-131 t1/2=8d) decay fast while others (Sr-90 t1/2=28.8yr) decay slow despite similar Q-values
chernobyl_relevance: Fundamental quantum field theory constant underlying all beta decays in Chernobyl isotopes; Fermi's original 1934 beta decay theory (now understood as W-boson exchange); the factor determining how long each radionuclide persists in the environment
source: Fermi 1934; Gamow-Teller vs Fermi transitions; Particle Data Group 2022

physics_detail: Sr²⁺ ion is chemical homolog of Ca²⁺; incorporated into hydroxyapatite [Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂] of bone replacing calcium; once incorporated, remains for bone turnover timescale; effective half-life: combination of radioactive (28.8 yr) and biological (~18 yr bone); Sr-90 delivers chronic dose to red bone marrow throughout life
chernobyl_relevance: Sr-90 ingested in contaminated water/food → gut absorption → blood → bone deposition; marrow irradiation from Sr-90 beta can cause leukemia/aplastic anemia; DOSE to marrow from bone-surface Sr-90 is much higher than dose to soft tissue; this is why Sr-90 ingestion dose coefficient (2.8E-08 Sv/Bq) >> external dose coefficient
source: ICRP 67 1993 bone seekers; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv; Snyder 1975; Leggett 1992 Health Phys
